application_credentials.description: Nothing to add: the integration signs in through its own published Cloudflare OAuth client. Add a credential only to use a client of your own; it then replaces the built-in one. Create it in the Cloudflare dashboard under Manage Account → OAuth clients with redirect URL `{redirect_uri}`, grant types authorization code and refresh token, token endpoint authentication none (PKCE) and the scopes {scopes}; enter its client ID with an empty secret. [Cloudflare OAuth clients]({docs_oauth_clients}), [project notes]({more_info_url}).

user.title: Cloudflare Access
user.description: Puts the whole hostname behind Cloudflare Access: only people with a Home Assistant account get in, and voice assistants or MCP clients sign in through Access. Continue to sign in with Cloudflare; the consent page lists the permissions used. Use a desktop browser: the Android companion app cannot finish the return from the consent page.

account.title: Cloudflare account
account.description: The sign-in was granted for several accounts. Choose the one whose zone serves the hostname.

api_token.title: Cloudflare API token
api_token.description: An account-level token with the permissions 'Access: Apps and Policies: Edit' and 'Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups: Read'. Stored in the config entry.

settings.title: Hostname and options
settings.description: The gate starts off, so nothing changes at the edge until you switch it on in the options. Who gets in: every active Home Assistant user, by the e-mail address found on their account (login username, display name, or the field a login integration stores). Currently: {allowed_users}. A request Access lets through is served as the user who carries that address.

data.delete_objects_on_remove: Delete the Access applications when the integration is removed

data_description.hostname: The public hostname Cloudflare serves Home Assistant on, e.g. ha.example.com.
data_description.extra_bypass_paths: Path prefixes anyone can reach without logging in, for callers that can hold neither a cookie nor a token. Example: /api/webhook/abc for a webhook a third-party service posts to. Nothing is open unless listed. [Bypass policies]({docs_policies})
data_description.client_redirect_uris: Clients that find the OAuth server on their own (MCP clients such as Claude) may register only with a redirect URL listed here. Example: {example_mcp_redirect}, or {example_wildcard_redirect} for every path. A client that asks you for a client ID and secret is added under "Add OAuth client" instead. [Managed OAuth]({docs_managed_oauth})
data_description.service_token_ids: Client IDs of Access service tokens whose CF-Access-Client-Id and CF-Access-Client-Secret headers pass the gate. Example: a script on another machine that calls the API. [Service tokens]({docs_service_tokens})
data_description.session_duration: How long a login lasts before Access asks again; also the lifetime of a registered client's refresh token. Pick a value or type your own, e.g. 48h or 90m. [Session duration]({docs_session})
data_description.delete_objects_on_remove: Off keeps the gate and the registered clients in Cloudflare after the integration is removed, e.g. to adopt them from another Home Assistant instance.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in with Cloudflare again
reauth_confirm.description: Cloudflare no longer accepts the sign-in. Continue to sign in again.

error.invalid_auth: Cloudflare rejected the credential. It needs 'Access: Apps and Policies: Edit' on this account.
error.missing_org_read: The credential cannot read the Zero Trust organization (the team domain). It needs 'Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups: Read'.
error.api_error: Cloudflare returned an error; see the log.

error.invalid_redirect_uri: Redirect URLs must start with https://.
error.invalid_duration: Enter a number of hours or minutes, e.g. 720h or 30m.

abort.invalid_auth: Cloudflare rejected the credential. It needs 'Access: Apps and Policies: Edit' on this account.

abort.api_error: Cloudflare returned an error; see the log.
abort.no_accounts: The sign-in reaches no Cloudflare account with a Zero Trust organization. Select the account on Cloudflare's consent page, and set up Zero Trust in it first.

restart_required.title: Restart Home Assistant to accept clients authenticated by Cloudflare Access
restart_required.description: The integration was set up after the web server had started, so its authentication middleware could not be installed. Until Home Assistant is restarted, requests from token-bearing clients (Google Assistant, Alexa, MCP clients) that Cloudflare Access admitted are rejected by Home Assistant.

no_allowed_users.title: No Home Assistant user can pass the Cloudflare Access gate
no_allowed_users.description: No active Home Assistant user carries an e-mail address (as login username, display name, or in a login integration's credential), so there is nobody to list in the gate's allow policy. The policy was left as it was. Give a user an address, then reload the integration.

user.title: Register an OAuth client
user.description: For a client whose console asks for a client ID and secret: Google Home account linking, the Alexa skill, any service that cannot register itself. Access issues the credentials; the next page shows them with the URLs to enter in that console. Who may link is the gate's own allow rule.

data_description.name: Anything that identifies the client to you, e.g. Google Home.
data_description.redirect_uris: The callback URL(s) the client's console shows, e.g. {example_console_redirect}. Exact https:// URLs.

reconfigure.title: Change the OAuth client
reconfigure.description: Saving updates the registration in Access and shows the credentials again.
